claims.author: zzzi2p
claims.harm: a pool of 10 idle sessions doubles network resource usage
claims.quote: 10 standby sessions is a lot, except maybe at startup. If your I2P connections limit is 10, then you're doubling your network resource usage.

status_by.quote: reduce the pre-created sessions to 1, given the above.

claims.author: zzzi2p
claims.harm: starting many sessions at once at startup could trigger router tunnel build rate limits
claims.quote: The Java router has some tunnel build rate-limiting that may kick in.

status_by.quote: This PR is not going to create a storm of I2P sessions creation at startup because new session creation is not being done in a tight loop, deliberately.

claims.status_note: author explained sessions are not created in a tight loop and showed startup timings

claims.author: eyedeekay
claims.harm: holding a bank of 10 sessions is wasteful unless demand rate requires it
claims.quote: keeping a bank of 10 of them is pretty wasteful

status_by.quote: reduce the pre-created sessions to 1, given the above.

claims.author: mzumsande
claims.harm: extra sessions expire after 10 minutes and waste resources if not used before expiration
claims.quote: If we don't use these extra sessions before they expire, their creation would be a waste of ressources.

status_by.quote: reduce the pre-created sessions to 1, given the above.

claims.author: mzumsande
claims.quote: Maybe it could make a sense to fill the m_unused_i2p_sessions buffer with 4 connections right after startup?
claims.request: fill the unused sessions buffer with connections right after startup when using -onlynet=i2p

status_by.quote: given that opening of new connections is done serially, one after another (not in parallel), and occasionally (except during startup) maybe it would be best to pre-create just one session?

claims.status_note: author replied that serial connection opening makes pre-creating just one session preferable

claims.author: jonatack
claims.question: whether this change only applies when a node is configured with -i2pacceptincoming=0
claims.quote: If I understand correctly, this change is only for if a node is configured with -i2pacceptincoming=0 to not accept inbound I2P connections?

status_by.quote: Yes. That is because if it is accepting incoming connections (has a permanent listening I2P address) then there is just one I2P session which is associated with that address and that session is used for all incoming and outgoing connections.

claims.status_note: author confirmed because accepting inbound connections uses a single persistent session
